reason: I'll start with the biceps: muscle cells belong in the front space, and the chapter says the biceps bends the elbow.
expectation: I expect the cells to form a biceps in the front of the arm; I'm not sure exactly how they will be assembled.

alternatives.reason: Adding mineral would strengthen the front bone, but I want to build the muscle first.

effect: The cells formed a biceps, but the radius still needs mineral. I'll finish the front attachment next.
reaction: The time strip showing cells joining into long fibres made the assembly clearer.
reason: Adding mineral should strengthen the bone at the biceps attachment and advance the front-arm goal.
expectation: I expect mineral to be added to the radius, making it harder and better able to resist compression.

alternatives.reason: I could start the triceps, but I want to finish the front first.

effect: The front is complete, and the demonstration shows how the biceps pulls the radius to bend the elbow. I'll build the back next.
reaction: Seeing the pull turn the forearm made the attachment's purpose clearer.
reason: I'll add muscle cells to build the triceps, which the chapter says straightens the elbow.
expectation: I expect the cells to form a triceps between the back tendons, while the bone still needs mineral.

alternatives.reason: I could mineralize the back bone first, but I'd like to see the opposing muscle built.

effect: The triceps is in place, but the ulna still needs mineral to complete the back attachment.
reaction: The pull behind the elbow makes sense as the opposite arrangement to the biceps, though the assembly feels familiar.
reason: I'll add mineral to the ulna; it's the only available combination and should finish the back-arm goal.
expectation: I expect the bone to harden and a demonstration to show the triceps straightening the elbow.

effect: The back is complete. The demonstration shows how pulling behind the elbow straightens the arm, contrasting with the biceps pulling in front.
reaction: The matched demonstrations made the opposing muscle actions clear, though finishing the back repeated the front's assembly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Completing the front attachment was most worthwhile because the demonstration showed how the biceps pulls on the radius to bend the elbow.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the triceps felt somewhat repetitive after assembling the biceps, even though its position helped explain the opposite movement.

surprise.text: The same kind of muscle cells could produce opposite movements depending on where their tendons attach.

arbitrary.text: The fittings had clear purposes, though the mineral had to be added before the completed movement demonstration appeared.

continue.text: I'd choose to continue: seeing the two attachments turn a familiar elbow movement into something understandable made me curious about other body systems.
